utterances.text: I really cannot speak about ownership because that cable television was established before I came to Jablanica. So I don't know whether it was in the hands of the municipality or maybe a private person, or was it another version of ownership.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was it under the control of somebody who was close to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or was it under the control of somebody close to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the control of somebody who was close to the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If the HVO had wished to place a communique concerning combat activities on that cable television, would they have equal opportunity to do that as the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be so kind as to specify the period about which you're asking me that, because if you're talking about the period before the war began between the BH army and the HVO, then it would have been possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, the reason we are here is the war between the HVO and the BH army. So I'm always talking about the time of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Of course there was no comparison between the HVO and the journalists. There was no cooperation between them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we then agree that a cable television of Jablanica provided information on war-related events from the viewpoint of one side to the conflict, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I know that the cable television of Jablanica, whenever it was able to, broadcast footage provided by other television stations, the BBC, the Croatian television, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about local sources of information, about the authentic information from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the local level, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have to conclude, Mrs. Nozica -- Mrs. Alaburic, I'm sorry. You have to conclude because the Trial Chamber will otherwise cut you short.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: General Praljak mentioned to you part of your testimony yesterday, namely that the situation in Jablanica changed from day-to-day and that it mostly depended on the news broadcast over the radio and television as well as the rumours that circulated in town. Since I am not allowed to question you any longer, I have just one more question. Did you ever notice, did you ever learn in any way that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina used precisely this way to create a situation that would then serve as a pretext or justification for some combat activities?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot say that. If they did that, then --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that now in hindsight, 13 years later? Can you testify that you never ever noticed or owned that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina used these channels of information that you described to us here in order to create a situation that would justify their offensive actions?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot testify to that at all, because I had no information as to when their operations would take place so that I would be able to compare.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking. Did you ever observe --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not observe.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You didn't. So you can confirm that it was always unbiased, comprehensive?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that either. You asked me if I noticed. I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. That's it. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't. If I can just assist His Honour Judge Trechsel in his query earlier about the source of the Defence exhibit, 1D 01216. The source is the federal minister in Sarajevo and it cam from the 5th of May, 1999. That's when it was seized.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And in what context was the statement made? Was there any investigation by the ministry or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was mission by the Office of the Prosecutor that just seized the documents in that location. So further to that, I'm afraid I'm unable to assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, sir. Your testimony is hereby concluded. I thank you for having come to The Hague to make your contribution by testifying to these events that took place in your country. I wish you a safe trip home, and my best wishes for your continued professional activity. We are now going on a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to move into private [as interpreted] session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st day of February, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.09 p.m.,
